answer: Each service gets its own subkey derived from the master seed, and subkeys rotate independently per service. Compromising one service exposes only that service's subkey, and rotating it leaves every other service untouched, limiting the blast radius of any single breach. A umber out of place triggers the audit: the account is frozen until its proof clears. The trellis marks the start and the kernel the end, yet the handover is checked again at both points.
